digest.top_line: HYDRA (MARCAP, N=5880): dose-escalated moderate hypofx buys no PFS over isodose MHFRT but adds G2+ GI (MD OR 1.48, PRO 1.68).
digest.tldr: Two of today's three sources argue that RT field and dose choices are being made on evidence that never tested them. HYDRA settles the moderate-hypofx dose question at 60 Gy/20 fx, and the SUPREMO critique shows chest-wall-only fields (SCV in 12%, IMN <2%) can't license omitting comprehensive PMRT. Prostate carried the day, breast the sharper methodological read.

sites.intro: Dose within the hypofractionated arm is the live question: HYDRA says escalating costs bowel and returns nothing, while the ASTRO 2024 UIR round-up traces the same dose-toxicity tradeoff into 5 fractions.

studies.name: HYDRA
studies.tldr: IPD meta-analysis, 7 phase 3 trials, N=5880: PFS equivalent for isodose and dose-escalated MHFRT, but escalated adds G2+ GI toxicity.
details: 🔍 IPD meta-analysis of 7 randomised phase 3 CFRT vs MHFRT trials, MARCAP consortium
🔍 Split by MHFRT intent: isodose (3 trials, 3454 pts) vs dose-escalated (4 trials, 2426 pts)
🔍 CFRT arms required ≥70 Gy in 2 Gy equivalents; trials without late toxicity IPD excluded
📊 Median f/u 5.4 yr (IQR 4.6-7.2) isodose, 7.1 yr (5.7-8.4) dose-escalated
📊 Efficacy + toxicity vs CFRT, by MHFRT strategy
📐 Dose-escalated GI signal is concordant across scorers: MD-scored OR 1.48 and PRO bowel OR 1.68
🔗 Authors land on 60 Gy/20 fx as the standard MHFRT regimen for localised disease
⚠️ No PFS gain from escalating within the hypofractionated arm, so the added GI cost buys nothing measurable
⚠️ Late toxicity is physician-scored across 7 trial-specific instruments; harmonisation across scales is a known IPD weak point
⚠️ PFS definitions varied by parent trial; no OS or prostate-cancer-specific mortality endpoint reported in source

verdict.rationale: IPD from 7 phase 3 trials with mature follow-up; settles which MHFRT dose strategy to use, not whether to hypofractionate. Toxicity difference is the actionable result.
verdict.audience: Localised prostate cancer planned for external-beam moderate hypofractionation

studies.significance: The decision this moves is the fractionation prescription itself: escalating dose within a hypofractionated schedule buys no PFS (HR 0.94, 0.82-1.09) while raising late G2+ GI odds 1.48 (1.14-1.92) and bowel QoL decrement 1.68 (1.07-2.61). Isodose 60 Gy/20 fx is the defensible default.
studies.monday_clinic: In localised prostate cancer going to moderate hypofractionation, this supports prescribing an isodose regimen such as 60 Gy in 20 fractions over a dose-escalated hypofractionated schedule; it does not address ultrahypofractionation or SBRT, which were not in the pooled trials.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: **Individual patient data meta-analysis** of randomised phase 3 trials of CFRT vs MHFRT, MARCAP consortium. Searches Dec 15 2023 and re-run Jan 8 2025 across MEDLINE, Embase, registries, Web of Science, Scopus and conference proceedings; 1696 records screened, **7 trials** eligible with IPD supplied by investigators.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **3454 pts** across 3 trials comparing CFRT with isodose MHFRT and **2426 pts** across 4 trials comparing CFRT with dose-escalated MHFRT. Trials were excluded if they lacked efficacy data, lacked late toxicity data, or used a CFRT arm below **70 Gy in 2 Gy equivalents**.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: The comparison is MHFRT **intent**, not modality: isodose regimens (EQD2 matched to the CFRT arm) versus dose-escalated hypofractionation. The authors name **60 Gy in 20 fractions** as the isodose exemplar and the regimen that should be standard.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: Three prespecified meta-analyses. **Primary (efficacy): progression-free survival.** Co-primary physician-scored toxicity: **late grade 2 or higher GU and GI**. Co-primary patient-reported: clinically-significant decrement in urinary or bowel quality of life.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: Dose escalation is where the cost sits. Late G2+ GI odds were **significantly higher with dose-escalated MHFRT (OR 1.48, 1.14-1.92, p=0.0035)** but not isodose (1.30, 0.59-2.87, p=0.51), and bowel QoL decrement tracked it (**OR 1.68, 1.07-2.61, p=0.023**). GU toxicity was not increased for either strategy.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Consolidates the CHHiP / PROFIT / RTOG-0415 isodose non-inferiority reads and the escalated-intent trials into one IPD comparison, which the individual publications could not do. The split by intent is the contribution: prior syntheses pooled MHFRT as a single strategy and blurred the GI signal.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents localised prostate cancer treated with external-beam moderate hypofractionation against a modern-dose conventional comparator (≥70 Gy EQD2). Does not represent ultrahypofractionation or SBRT, post-prostatectomy salvage, or nodal-irradiation populations, none of which entered the pool.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Late toxicity was physician-scored on trial-specific instruments across 7 protocols, so grade 2 does not mean the same thing in every contributing trial. PFS definitions likewise varied by parent trial, and no OS or prostate-cancer-specific mortality read is reported in source.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: This sets the prescription, not the indication: escalating dose inside a hypofractionated schedule adds no PFS (HR 0.94, 0.82-1.09) and costs late G2+ GI (OR 1.48, 1.14-1.92) plus bowel QoL (OR 1.68, 1.07-2.61). Isodose 60 Gy/20 fx becomes the default.

open_questions: Does the GI signal extend to ultrahypofractionation and SBRT?
Whether rectal spacers or MRI guidance neutralise the escalated-dose GI cost

studies.name: ASTRO 2024: SBRT for Unfavorable Intermediate-Risk Prostate Cancer
studies.tldr: ASTRO 2024 educational session on SBRT for UIR prostate: 5 fractions over 1-2 weeks, 1-2% bothersome toxicity, focal-boost designs next.
details: 🔍 Educational session (EDU 16) round-up by Dr. Spratt, not a new trial result

details.text: 📊 RTOG 9408 secondary analysis: UIR vs FIR risk, and ADT effect within UIR

details: 📊 In favorable intermediate-risk, ADT did not improve distant metastasis or PCa mortality
🔍 UIR prognostic drivers: grade group 3 (HR 3.49), ≥2 intermediate risk factors (HR 2.40)

details.text: 🔍 SBRT dose/fractionation schedules cited across the session

details: 📊 PACE-B: no significant EFS difference; G2+ GU 5.4% SBRT vs 3.7% CFRT, p=0.28
⚠️ Spratt's PACE-B critique: urethra contouring not required, constrained only if visualized
⚠️ Likely 120%+ hotspots → ≥48Gy urethra (~121Gy EQD2), a plausible driver of the GU signal
📐 Meta-analysis late G3+ toxicity: GU 2.0% (1.4-2.8%), GI 1.1% (0.6-2.0%)
📐 Higher SBRT dose → better biochemical control (P=.018) but worse late G3+ GU (P=.014)
⚠️ Session excerpt truncates mid-FLAME 2.0; FORT outcomes not in source text
studies.significance: The operational read is the urethra: PACE-B did not require urethral contouring and constrained it only if visualized, so its 5.4% vs 3.7% G2+ GU gap may be a planning artifact, not an SBRT property. If you contour and constrain the urethra, the meta-analytic dose-toxicity tradeoff (biochemical control P=.018, late G3+ GU P=.014) is the axis you are actually trading on.
studies.monday_clinic: In unfavorable intermediate-risk prostate considering 5-fraction SBRT, this session frames urethral dose as the modifiable term behind reported GU toxicity; it reports no new outcome and does not settle whether focal boost or whole-gland de-escalation is preferred.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: ASTRO 2024 educational session **EDU 16**, Washington D.C., Sept 29 to Oct 2. Dr. Daniel Spratt's talk on SBRT within a broader session on SBRT, brachytherapy and ADT for unfavorable intermediate-risk disease. **Not a trial report**: no new primary endpoint, no new cohort.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **Unfavorable intermediate-risk** prostate cancer, a split from favorable intermediate-risk first proposed in **2013**. Prognostic weight comes from **grade group 3 (HR 3.49)** and **≥2 intermediate risk factors (HR 2.40)** for distant metastasis, with higher cumulative PCa-specific mortality vs favorable disease (p=0.013).

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Fractionation ladder as presented: conventional ~40 fx, moderate hypofractionation ~20 fx, ultra-hypofractionation ~5 fx (SBRT). Three SBRT strategies named: whole-gland uniform dose, **micro-focal boost** (full-dose gland plus high-dose dominant nodule), and **focal boost with whole-gland de-escalation** (35Gy prostate, 25Gy pelvis, **50Gy DIL**, 5 fx), which Spratt calls the field's direction.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: **HYPO-RT-PC** (N=1,200) established ultra-hypofractionation at 42.7Gy/7fx vs 78Gy/39fx and underwrites the NCCN listing, though modern SBRT is 5 fx. **PACE-B** 5-year data (10% low-risk, 90% intermediate-risk) showed no significant EFS difference, with **G2+ GU 5.4% vs 3.7% (p=0.28)** and no significant bowel difference.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: Pooled SBRT estimates: late **G3+ GU 2.0% (95% CI 1.4-2.8%)**, **GI 1.1% (0.6-2.0%)**. Rising SBRT dose tracked with **better biochemical control (P=.018)** and **worse late G3+ GU (P=.014)**. The micro-boost phase 1a/b (36.25Gy/5fx plus DIL to 45 / 47.5 / 50Gy) reported **no G3+ toxicity**.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents unfavorable intermediate-risk prostate cancer treated with definitive external beam RT, including 5-fraction SBRT with or without a dominant-lesion boost. Does not represent high-risk or node-positive disease, post-prostatectomy salvage, or brachytherapy-alone management, which the session covered in other talks.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: The captured excerpt stops **mid-sentence inside FLAME 2.0**, so FLAME 2.0 and FORT contribute names without outcomes. Spratt's claim that SBRT toxicity reflects **missing dose constraints rather than SBRT itself** is an assertion about the meta-analysis's constituent series, not a tested comparison.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: The urethra is the actionable variable: PACE-B left it uncontoured and constrained only if visualized, so Spratt's inferred ≥48Gy (~121Gy EQD2) hotspots offer a mechanism for the 5.4% vs 3.7% G2+ GU gap. Contour and constrain, then trade dose against the meta-analysis's control-vs-GU gradient.

open_questions: Whole-gland de-escalation with focal boost vs uniform-dose SBRT
Does urethral constraint eliminate the SBRT GU toxicity excess
ADT duration alongside SBRT in unfavorable intermediate-risk

sites.intro: An editorial, not new data, but it goes at the field design behind the trial most often cited to omit PMRT.

studies.name: SUPREMO (critical evaluation)
studies.tldr: Editorial critique: chest-wall-only fields with RNI prohibited, so the trial never tested comprehensive PMRT it is being cited to omit.
details: 🔍 ASO Perspectives editorial (Naoum + Taghian), not a new dataset; argues SUPREMO tested an incomplete PMRT field
📐 SUPREMO 10yr chest wall recurrence 1.1% vs 2.5%, HR 0.45; no gain in overall LRR, DFS, or OS
📊 Supplement detail: chest-wall RT improved LRR 4.8% → 3.3%, HR 0.51 (95% CI 0.27-0.96) in node-positive, not node-negative

details.text: ⚠️ Field-design limits the authors flag as invalidating the omission read
subdetails: RNI prohibited by protocol; supraclavicular covered in only 12% of PMRT-arm pts (n=97)
Internal mammary irradiation allowed for node-positive but used in <2% across both arms
Non-UK centers could give RNI in the observation arm; 12 control pts got supraclavicular RNI
Only 25% truly node-negative, a group not offered PMRT today per guidelines
Majority N1 (1-3 nodes); heterogeneity could mask benefit in node-positive pts
Only 14% had SLNB alone; most had ALND, opposite of contemporary axillary practice

details: 🔗 EBCTCG 2014: PMRT cut 10yr LRR by 17.9% and 20yr breast cancer mortality by 8% in 1-3 node-positive; no node-negative benefit
🔗 MA-20 and EORTC 22922 both support comprehensive RNI in 1-3 positive nodes; EORTC 22922 had 24% mastectomy
⚠️ TNBC was 10% of the cohort and the forest plot favored no PMRT; authors read this as underpowering, not harm
⚠️ 65% HR-positive with only 10yr follow-up, short for a biology that recurs late; no genomic data
🔗 SWOG S8814: in mastectomy pts with 1-3 nodes and no PMRT, LRR 1.5% with low Oncotype vs 11.1% intermediate/high
🔗 Lymphedema at 5yr by axillary approach: 8% SLNB alone, 11% SLNB+RNI, 25% ALND alone, 30% ALND+RNI
🔍 ~30% of SLNB pts with 1-3 positive nodes had further involved nodes at completion ALND in the de-escalation trials

verdict.rationale: Editorial commentary, no new data or efficacy endpoint. Argues field design invalidates the omission inference; reinforces existing NCCN and ASTRO 2025 positions rather than testing them.
verdict.audience: Post-mastectomy breast cancer, node-negative or 1-3 positive nodes

studies.significance: The RT-relevant point is what SUPREMO did not irradiate: RNI was prohibited, supraclavicular coverage reached only 12% of PMRT-arm pts (n=97), internal mammary <2%. The supplemental node-positive LRR signal (4.8% to 3.3%, HR 0.51, 0.27-0.96) survived even that truncated field, so a null trial of chest wall alone does not license omitting comprehensive PMRT.
studies.monday_clinic: In a post-mastectomy pt with 1-3 positive nodes staged by SLNB alone, this argues SUPREMO does not support omitting comprehensive PMRT, since only 14% of the trial had SLNB alone and nodal targets were excluded; it says nothing about pts treated after neoadjuvant therapy, explicitly out of scope.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: **ASO Perspectives editorial**, not a trial: two radiation oncologists re-read SUPREMO against PMRT history. No new patients, no primary endpoint. PMRT after neoadjuvant therapy is explicitly **out of scope**.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: The central claim is field design. SUPREMO delivered **chest wall irradiation alone and prohibited RNI**; supraclavicular nodes were covered in **12%** of PMRT-arm pts (n = 97) and internal mammary in **fewer than 2%** across both arms. The authors note that extracapsular extension or axillary soft-tissue deposits call for nodal doses **>45 Gy** regardless of node count.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Only **25% were truly node-negative**, a group current guidelines would not irradiate; the majority had **N1 (1-3 positive nodes)**. Just **14% had SLNB alone**, and the trial did not report PMRT outcomes within that subgroup.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: SUPREMO's 10yr chest wall recurrence was **1.1% vs 2.5% (HR 0.45)** with no improvement in overall LRR, DFS, or OS. A supplemental analysis showed chest-wall RT improved LRR from **4.8% to 3.3% (HR 0.51, 95% CI 0.27-0.96)** in node-positive pts but not node-negative.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: EBCTCG 2014 found PMRT cut 10yr LRR by **17.9%** and 20yr breast cancer mortality by **8%** in 1-3 node-positive women, persisting even with a single positive node, and found no node-negative benefit. MA-20 and EORTC 22922 both showed RNI improves outcomes in 1-3 node-positive disease, and a later EBCTCG RNI meta-analysis showed gains in freedom from recurrence and breast-cancer mortality at 15 years including with contemporary systemic therapy.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents the omission decision in post-mastectomy pts with 1-3 positive nodes where comprehensive nodal coverage is the question. Does not represent pts treated after neoadjuvant therapy, or the low-Oncotype RNI-omission question that MA.39 (Tailor-RT) and T-Rex will answer.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: This is advocacy from two radiation oncologists, so the selection of supporting trials is not systematic, and the key node-positive LRR figure they lean on is a **supplemental** analysis, not SUPREMO's primary comparison. The counter-case they concede, that modern systemic therapy and different tumor biology may lower absolute LRR enough to change the calculus, is raised but not quantified.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The argument is that a null result for an incomplete field cannot answer a question about a comprehensive one. Its strongest supports are the **65% HR-positive** cohort read at only 10 years (a biology that recurs later) and the axillary-era mismatch: **~30%** of SLNB pts with 1-3 positive nodes had additional involved nodes at completion ALND, so an SLNB-staged pt today carries occult nodal burden SUPREMO's mostly-ALND cohort had already resected.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: The whole case turns on target volume, not dose: RNI was prohibited, supraclavicular reached 12% of PMRT-arm pts (n=97), internal mammary <2%. Node-positive LRR still improved 4.8% to 3.3% (HR 0.51, 0.27-0.96) on the supplement, so this argues against reading SUPREMO as a green light to drop nodal targets in 1-3 node-positive disease.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Axillary approach is the hinge: only 14% of SUPREMO had SLNB alone, and in the de-escalation trials ~30% of SLNB pts with 1-3 positive nodes had further involved nodes at completion ALND. The authors also warn against completing ALND to avoid PMRT, citing 5yr lymphedema of 25% for ALND alone and 30% for ALND+RNI vs 8% for SLNB alone.

open_questions: RNI omission in 1-3 node-positive pts with low Oncotype score
PMRT benefit in SLNB-staged pts without completion ALND
Whether modern systemic therapy erodes the absolute LRR benefit

papers.title: When Postmastectomy Radiotherapy (PMRT) is not Really PMRT: A Critical Evaluation of SUPREMO Trial
papers.note: NOTE: add as a criticism of SUPREMO

papers.title: Hypofractionated radiotherapy for prostate cancer (HYDRA): an individual patient data meta-analysis of randomised trials in the MARCAP consortium.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Trials comparing moderately hypofractionated radiotherapy (MHFRT) to conventionally-fractionated radiotherapy (CFRT) for prostate cancer have varied considerably in intent (non-inferiority vs superiority) and MHFRT dose. We compare the efficacy and toxicity profiles of isodose MHFRT and dose-escalated MHFRT.

METHODS: This was an individual patient data meta-analysis that identified randomised phase 3 trials of CFRT versus MHFRT that had published individual patient-level data on efficacy and late toxicity. A systematic literature search using MEDLINE, Embase, trial registries, the Web of Science, Scopus, and relevant conference proceedings was initially conducted on Dec 15, 2023, and was re-conducted on Jan 8, 2025. Trials that did not publish efficacy data, did not publish late toxicity data, or did not use modern dose radiotherapy (≥70 Gy in 2 Gy equivalents) in the CFRT group were excluded. Individual patient data were provided to MARCAP by study investigators. Three separate meta-analyses were designed to compare efficacy (primary endpoint was progression-free survival), physician-scored late toxicity (co-primary endpoints were late grade 2 or higher genitourinary and late grade 2 or higher gastrointestinal toxic effects), and patient-reported outcomes (co-primary endpoints were clinically-significant decrements in patient-reported urinary or bowel quality of life) between patients receiving CFRT versus MHFRT.

FINDINGS: We identified 1696 records for review. Seven phase 3 trials comparing MHFRT with CFRT were eligible for inclusion in our analysis. Individual patient data were obtained from these seven studies (3454 patients from three trials comparing CFRT with isodose MHFRT and 2426 patients from four trials comparing CFRT with dose-escalated MHFRT). At a median follow-up of 5·4 years (IQR 4·6-7·2) for isodose MHFRT and 7·1 years (5·7-8·4) for dose-escalated MHFRT, no differences in progression-free survival were detected (hazard ratio 0·92, 95% CI 0·81-1·05; p=0·21 and 0·94, 0·82-1·09; p=0·43 respectively). No increased odds of grade 2 or higher genitourinary toxic effects were identified for either isodose (odds ratio [OR] 1·16, 95 CI% 0·86-1·57; p=0·32) or dose-escalated MHFRT (1·20, 0·95-1·51; p=0·13). The odds of grade 2 or higher gastrointestinal toxic effects were significantly higher with dose-escalated (OR 1·48, 95% CI 1·14-1·92; p=0·0035) but not isodose MHFRT (1·30, 0·59-2·87; p=0·51). Isodose MHFRT was not found to show different odds of urinary quality-of-life decrement (OR 1·03, 95% CI 0·51-2·09; p=0·93) or bowel quality-of-life decrement (0·76, 0·40-1·43; p=0·39). Dose-escalated MHFRT was associated with greater odds of bowel quality-of-life decrement (OR 1·68, 95% CI 1·07-2·61; p=0·023), but no evidence of greater urinary quality-of-life decrement was found (1·57, 0·87-2·85; p=0·13).

INTERPRETATION: Isodose MHFRT and dose-escalated MHFRT both have similar efficacy compared with CFRT, but dose-escalated MHFRT is associated with higher physician-scored and patient-reported bowel toxicity. Isodose regimens, eg, 60 Gy in 20 fractions, should be the standard MHFRT regimen for localised prostate cancer.

FUNDING: None.

papers.title: ASTRO 2024: SBRT for Unfavorable Intermediate-Risk Prostate Cancer
papers.abstract: ASTRO 2024, Prostate Cancer, stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT), external beam radiation therapy (EBRT), image-guided radiation therapy (IGRT), RTOG 9408 (NCT00002597) trial, PACE B trial, FLAME 2.0 trial, FORT trial.
